title: Jebel Irhoud (Middle Stone Age hominin site, Morocco)
note: Karst cave exposed by mining in the 1960s; INSAP/MPI-EVA excavations from 2004; TL 315 ± 34 ka (Richter et al. 2017), Irhoud 1-15 specimen list (Hublin et al. 2017 Extended Data Table 1). Coordinates PBDB 42866 and GeoNames 2545660 differ by ~1 km (mountain, not cave): needs a precise site coordinate. Reportedly classed Moroccan national heritage (press, unverified).

title: Omo Kibish Formation (Omo I and Omo II, Ethiopia)
note: Omo I found 1967 by Richard Leakey's team (Smithsonian); minimum age 233 ± 22 ka from Shala Qi2 tephra (Vidal et al. 2022, PMC8791829); earlier 195/197 ka (McDougall et al. 2005/2008). Needs better coordinates than PBDB 21715 (1977 catalogue).

title: Florisbad spring site and hominin cranium (South Africa)
note: Spring mound ~45 km NNW of Bloemfontein (PBDB 198625, 28°46.09'S 26°04.17'E); 1932 cranium; ESR 259 ± 35 ka on a molar (Grün et al. 1996) disputed by Berger & Hawks (2020 preprint; Homo 2023). Florisbad Quaternary Research Station (National Museum Bloemfontein). Contested record.

title: Onset of the Middle Stone Age in Africa
note: Levallois MSA by ~300 ka at Jebel Irhoud and Olorgesailie (Kenya), before 275 ± 6 ka at Gademotta (Ethiopia), before 284 ± 12 ka Kapthurin, before 291 ± 45 ka Kathu Pan (Richter et al. 2017; Scerri et al. 2018). Olorgesailie 2018 Science papers (Brooks, Deino, Potts) are the next sources to open.

title: Homo naledi
note: Rising Star cave system, Cradle of Humankind; ~335–236 ka (Scerri et al. 2018 citing Dirks et al. 2017 eLife, open access). Contemporary with early H. sapiens in southern Africa; burial claims contested.

title: Herto Homo sapiens fossils (Middle Awash, Ethiopia)
note: H. sapiens idaltu (White et al. 2003 Nature); ~160–155 ka (Vidal et al. 2022). Among the most widely accepted fully modern crania.

title: Middle Pleistocene green Sahara episodes
note: Richter et al. 2017 cite a marked but short humid episode around 330 ka enabling north/sub-Saharan continuity; needs the underlying paleoclimate source (their ref. 29) and a sea-core dataset.
